## ELI5

Read the message files that older OpenCode sessions actually use, so saved conversations regain their prompts and replies in History and conversation search, and refresh when separate parts change.

## What Changed

- Load separately stored message parts when inline content is absent, using the producer’s part-ID order.
- Convert text, reasoning and tool parts into the existing transcript shapes; retain older records that already contain inline content.
- Reuse the existing JSON read, cancellation and WSL handling, and reject message IDs that could escape the expected part directory.
- Apply one-time repairs only to OpenCode JSON parse rows and search cursors. SQLite-backed OpenCode sessions and other agents retain their existing entries.
- Track a separate signature of message/part paths, sizes, mtimes and ctimes. Keep the parent session file’s real mtime, size and read offsets.
- Persist and compare that signature across History, Search, worker snapshots and failed-version retries. Add nullable columns within locked migrations, retaining existing cache data.

## Why

OpenCode’s legacy MessageV2 JSON format stores message metadata under `storage/message/<sessionId>` and content under `storage/part/<messageId>`. Orca still discovers these JSON sessions, but the parser looked only for inline content. This produces empty prompts and transcripts. Existing parse-cache rows and current search cursors can preserve that omission even after the reader is corrected. Later writes to separate message or part files can also leave the parent session JSON unchanged, so retained JSON candidates need their own dependency revision.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #50642

## Visual Proof

N/A

No graphical layout or interaction component changes. The following before/after results come from the affected production operation with the same fixture input.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| firstUserPrompt is absent and separately stored bodies are omitted. Previously cached empty previews and current search cursors survive a parser-only fix. | The prompt is “Inspect the build failure.\nKeep the command output.” Replies, reasoning, tool calls/results and the inline control are emitted. Only affected JSON cache rows/cursors are invalidated once; SQLite-backed sessions and other agents remain intact. |
| An assistant part changes from `draftquery` to same-length `finalquery` after both caches restart, while the parent stat stays unchanged. History remains stale and conversation Search misses the new text. | History shows `finalquery` and Search finds it. A later dependent-content revision receives a fresh retry budget and becomes searchable after previous read failures. |

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally through the production-entry reproductions described below
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] Every added test fails without this change and avoids the test anti-patterns

Persisted transcript, import-parser and search-index data integrity. The fixture uses real files and SQLite rather than replacing internal parser/storage chains.

The original two regression tests pass. The producer-shaped filesystem fixture failed on the original parser. With that reader corrected, a separate baseline check reproduced the stale real-SQLite parse row until its repair was added. The search migration regression failed with the JSON cursor still at 100; the fix sets it to the existing partial-file sentinel -1 while SQLite/Claude controls stay at 100. A later cursor of 200 survives reopening, proving the repair is one-time.

The dependency-freshness follow-up passes 6 targeted tests across 5 files, including a same-length assistant-part rewrite after both persistent caches restart and recovery after held-out failures. Its previous-head baseline fails the preview, Search and retry assertions. Two additional validation-only old-schema probes preserve indexed/parse rows and prove rollback after a real SQLite trigger rejects migration metadata. The actual migration functions also pass six concurrent two-connection rounds, adding each column once. All seven blocking-I/O ratchets pass without an allowance increase; changed-code quality reports zero findings across 147 integrated paths.

Reproduce the focused tests with:

```sh
pnpm test src/main/ai-vault/scanners/opencode/session-scanner-opencode-json-parts.test.ts src/main/ai-vault/scanners/opencode/session-scanner-opencode-freshness.test.ts src/main/ai-vault-search/storage/session-search-opencode-parts-repair.test.ts src/main/ai-vault/parse-cache/session-parse-cache-persistence.test.ts src/main/ai-vault-search/indexing/session-search-unchanged-reread.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

Locally executed through the repository’s test-runtime runner on Linux with Node 24.22.3. macOS, Windows and remote SSH execution are not claimed.

Final integrated validation: 32 focused regression tests in 22 files passed, including the unchanged archive-write failure case that had timed out under earlier heavy concurrent checking. The Drive performance contract passed separately (1 file/1 test). Changed-code quality passed with zero new findings across 129 changed paths; final touched-file formatting and git diff --check passed. Node typechecking passed for 17,026 files and web typechecking for 16,094 files using the repository-supported Bun compiler with one worker. These are aggregate validation results for the prepared contributions, not per-PR test counts.

Initial local `check:changed` attempts stopped during workspace-package build because this environment rejected the tsx CLI IPC socket (`listen EPERM`); a later attempt hit `ENOSPC` when pnpm automatically rebuilt native dependencies. The default tsrs typechecker was also terminated with SIGKILL; the supported Bun typechecking route completed successfully. No complete local gate pass is claimed.

Current candidate `e6fa4c61b8b59656d8f1e41b15192fa9b5f8f7c6` passed the [complete required `pnpm check:changed` gate in exact-source fork CI](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45974662879/job/140423293200). The job checked the candidate against `9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817`, verified both commit IDs, and confirmed that validation left tracked sources unchanged.

## Performance

The legacy JSON reader now performs the part-file reads required to recover omitted content; inline messages skip those reads. Sorting follows the producer’s storage-key order. Marker-gated cache/search repairs cause one reread of affected JSON sessions, preserving SQLite-backed sessions and unrelated agents.

Discovery now lists and stats the actual message/part files for each retained legacy JSON candidate, after SQLite duplicate filtering. Each unique retained session is fingerprinted once per discovery, with at most four sessions observed concurrently. This adds metadata I/O; fingerprinting does not read JSON bodies. Unchanged signatures remain eligible for History and Search reuse. Candidate ordering and retention still use the real parent-file stat.

## Risk

**Level:** Medium

The sensitive path is historical JSON storage while part files are missing or being written. Existing guarded file reads and cancellation behavior are reused, and older inline content remains authoritative. Repair markers touch derived cache/search state only; original session and part files are unchanged. A revert restores the old reader but does not reinstate invalidated cache rows or previous cursors; normal scans rebuild derived data.

The optional signature columns are added without rebuilding either cache. One writer transaction protects the parse-cache schema and scope-version update; the Search column migration uses its existing writer lock. Failed migration writes roll back, and simultaneous openers check columns after acquiring that lock. Unreadable dependency observations are reported for retry rather than accepted as a fresh revision.

## AI Disclosure

Core contribution owner: @Afloat16. Required tooling disclosure: GPT-6 Astra Pro was used for implementation and review.

## Review

Reviewed the actual MessageV2 producer, part ordering, content conversion and persisted upgrade behavior. Existing path joining and host/WSL restrictions remain in use; message IDs with separators are rejected. SQLite-backed OpenCode parsing, other agents, SSH routing and mobile wire shapes are unchanged. No new polling or graphical layout code is added; dependency fingerprinting adds metadata observations only for retained legacy JSON candidates.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable: this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments or documentation.

## Notes

MessageV2.parts(messageID) reads Storage.list([part, messageID]) and sorts by part ID; get() reads metadata separately. Reviewed related first-prompt, native-chat, WSL and cache-version work; those changes did not load these legacy JSON message bodies.

Primary references:

- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.1.15/packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.1.15/packages/opencode/src/session/index.ts
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.1.15/packages/opencode/src/storage/storage.ts

- [x] Before/after data evidence is included, with `N/A` and a reason for graphical proof

- [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote and path/shortcut impact considered
